title: Feed the starter
thesis: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it.

nodes.text: Team leads reward what they can see, but the result is decided upstream, before anyone looks, the way bread fails twelve hours before the dough is touched.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 5: failure happened twelve hours before they touched the dough

nodes.text: The shape fails if the problem stays abstract. What team-side moment makes a team lead recognise it? The brief gives none (slot e2).
Rush the groundwork and the failure can't be fixed at the end, and the people who rushed never learn why.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 5: 'nobody can fix that at the oven'; rushers 'never understand why their bread fails'

nodes.text: Protect a stretch of slow work on purpose: the bakery's first month of feeding the starter, with no loaves shaped.
Keep a record of the slow part so you can read back instead of guessing.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 7: eleven years of notebooks above the ovens

nodes.text: 'It's hazing.' Her best baker thought so too, until week three, when he noticed the rain slowing the rise.
The first step for a team lead on Monday.
What is the concrete first step? The brief's purpose ('protect the unglamorous early work') names the goal but not the action.
